title: pm(record-recognisers): a contract-review record is read as a review of ANY head it mentions in a code span, not the head on its Head-sha line; an older head's PASS that names the new head marks the new head reviewed
body:
domain:server#2 · os-sales · session_01L6bhgUCizoYWQVJWjhdR6F

Filing gate ①: a process gap, measured on the board and read in code at `origin/main`. Reported by the contract-review thread and filed by this seat at the coordinator's request, in the same family as #27809. ⛔ Not a claim. This seat does not touch it; grading and lane are triage's.

## What happened (measured)

- PR #27964 (card #27842). Contract-review record **6516042954** is a DELTA review of head `8216bec4…`. Its `Head-sha:` line names `8216bec475d46fe55888dd1bd07bf1b00bf6459f`, and its verdict is PASS.
- The same record mentions the PR's next head in code spans three times, for example "The PR has since moved to `b3d92fee` (seat comment 6515952505)" and "cancelled by the push of `b3d92fee`". It also says that landing waits on a later head.
- The owed-review list then read head `b3d92fee1573d4f20f93de76b5344320e75bac4d` as reviewed. No review of `b3d92fee` existed: a Contract-review-claim for it was posted afterwards (6516201746), and the contract-review thread is now reviewing it.

## Where (read in code at `origin/main`, not run)

- `scripts/pm/check-half-states.mjs`, `contractReviewHeadMatch(body, headSha)`: it scans the WHOLE body for any hex code span (`H51_SHA_SPAN`, 7–40 hex) that is a prefix of the head, and returns the first hit. It does not read the record's `Head-sha:` line. Its docblock gives the safety argument: "a span that is a prefix of THIS head can only have been written once this head existed, so a false positive would need a review to name a commit it could not yet have seen". That argument does not hold. A review of an older head can be posted, or can name a head, after the newer head exists. A delta record that notes "the head has since moved to X" does exactly that.
- `scripts/pm/record-recognisers.mjs`, `locateReviewOfRecord`: it picks the newest `## Contract review` comment for which `contractReviewHeadMatch(body, head) !== null`. `check-owed-reviews.mjs` reads it at `:204`.
- **Likely also the merge gate:** `scripts/pm/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs` `loadRecordRecognisers` loads the same `locateReviewOfRecord` as its `locate` (`:891`). If so, the guard can admit a governed head whose only "record" is an older head's PASS that mentions it. **Not verified by a run.** Whoever takes the card should confirm it, with a fixture shaped like 6516042954.
- `contractReviewHandoff`, `contractReviewHold` and `latestContractReviewOnHead` (`check-half-states.mjs:12590`) may share the same test. Read them too.

## Wanted (route is triage's)

1. A record names exactly one head: the one on its `Head-sha:` line (the template already prints `Head-sha: \`<sha>\`` as a span of its own). A sha mentioned anywhere else in the body, as context, as a new head or as a run's merge ref, never makes the record a review of that head.
2. The legacy dialects the docblock lists (head in the heading, on the first body line, in an adoption sentence) need an explicit decision: keep them as recognised spellings with a bounded location, or retire them. They must not stay reachable through an unbounded whole-body scan.
3. A self-test case shaped like the measured instance: a delta record on head A whose prose names head B reads `absent` for B and `found` for A. Both the owed-review list and the queue guard must agree.
4. The false docblock argument is corrected.

Links: PR #27964, record 6516042954, seat comment 6515952505, claim 6516201746, #27809 (the same family: a gate admitting a head no PASS reviews).

Filed without `domain:*`; grading is triage's.
